seen_animation: A line-drawn duck stands on a ground line in front of grey zigzag mountains. Frames 1-2: the duck is in profile, head and beak pointing left, body hump to the right, two legs with triangular feet. Frame 3: the head turns toward the viewer, a three-quarter head with the beak pointing down. Frames 4-15: the head is fully frontal (octagonal head, two dot eyes, a narrow beak hanging down over the chest) while the body and legs stay in the same pose. From frame 6 small teardrop shapes appear: at both sides of the beak (6, 10), on the chest and belly (7, 9, 11, 12), and at the feet (8, 9, 12, 13), so the drops read as tears falling from the face to the ground. Frames 14-15: no drops, the duck stands still facing front. Frame 16: the head turns back to profile facing left, as in frame 1.
seen_film: A clay bird stands centered on a flat ground with a blurred landscape behind it. Frames 1-2: the head is turned to the viewer's left, long beak pointing left. Frame 3: the head has turned to face the camera. Frames 4-15: it faces the camera with drooping eyes and the beak pointing down; from frame 6 white teardrops appear at the beak, run down the chest and drop to the ground between the feet (6-12). Frames 13-15: drops stop, the bird stands facing front. Frame 16: a blurred frame as the head turns back to the left.
named_subject: a duck (the doodle's duck) that turns to face the viewer and cries
evidence: Head turn matches the film's timing: profile left in 1-2 (film 1-2), turned in 3 (film 3), frontal 4-15 (film 4-15), back to profile left in 16 (film 16 blurred turn). Tears start in frame 6 at the beak in both, are on the chest in 7-12 and at the feet in 8-13, and stop by 14-15 in both. Body, legs and feet stay at the same frame position throughout with no doubling, and frame 3 supplies an in-between three-quarter head between profile and front.
primary_gap: The 15 to 16 return to profile happens in a single step from the full frontal octagon head to the full profile head with no intermediate head shape, and the frontal head is a new octagonal construction that the doodle never drew, attached to a body that stays in profile.
closes_when: A three-quarter head like frame 3 appears in frame 16 (or frame 15 begins the turn), and the frontal head keeps the doodle's rounded head outline with the beak drawn as the doodle's open two-line wedge seen from the front rather than a closed rectangle.
protect: The exact timing of the turn (2 to 3) and the tear sequence (6 through 13); the drawn teardrops travelling from beak to chest to feet; the unchanged body, legs and feet position; the doodle's thin straight-segment strokes and its profile body silhouette in frames 1-2 and 16; the stable scenery.
identity_gap: Frames 1-2 and 16 are the c.png duck (mirrored), but the frontal head in 4-15 is an invented octagon with dot eyes and a rectangular beak that is drawn in the doodle's stroke style but not derived from its head shape.
